scope: Only actually opted-in profile gates are qualified; this is separate from whole-case success and is not a matched baseline comparison.

vo_clt_ct036_v1_paired_lobes.evidence: The bodice upper edge has two rounded teal arcs, one on each side of the central front depression. Each arc continues into the same worn dress boundary.

vo_clt_ct036_v1_center_dip.evidence: The two neckline arcs visibly meet at the center dip above the bodice's central seam. It is not a printed heart or a straight-sided isolated V neckline.

vo_clt_ct109_v2_visible_relation.evidence: The chain forms a V across the wearer's upper chest and a rectangular silver pendant hangs at its center, attached to that neck chain rather than placed nearby.

vo_clt_ct116_v1_bail_pendant.evidence: The rectangular pendant has a tiny top connector, but the native crop does not establish a separately recognizable bail loop attached at the top. Its geometry is only a few pixels and remains ambiguous.

vo_clt_ct116_v1_chain_loop.evidence: The neck chain reaches the pendant region, but its passage through an open bail aperture is not resolved at 1024×1536 native scale. Continuity near the top connector is not sufficient proof of through-loop contact.

vo_clt_ct001_v1_partway_down.evidence: The ochre pullover has a collarless round neck and a visible short center-front button placket that terminates within the front body.

vo_clt_ct008_v1_visible_relation.evidence: Raised crossed and braided yarn columns repeat over the ochre torso panel; they have local relief and are not a flat rope print.

vo_clt_ct044_v1_neck_underarm.evidence: PARTIAL at native scale: Sloped knit lines are present around the shoulders, but an uninterrupted construction seam from neckline through to underarm cannot be distinguished confidently from cable pattern and sleeve folds at native resolution.

vo_clt_ct057_v1_visible_relation.evidence: PARTIAL at native scale: The charcoal front waist has a dark tied cord bow and hanging ends. Both separate cord exit openings and their casing attachment are not unambiguously resolved in the dark waist region.

vo_clt_ct114_v2_visible_relation.evidence: The pale-green oval stone has a closed continuous silver rim around its perimeter, visibly separate from the interior stone. The small beaded surface of the rim does not break its encircling boundary; no gem grade or hidden safety claim is inferred.
